parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State and explain the trend observed in the thermal stability of the Group 2 nitrates.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Lead(II) nitrate, $\text{Pb}(\text{NO}_3)_2$, decomposes on heating in a similar manner to the Group 2 nitrates.

Write an equation for the decomposition of lead(II) nitrate.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest how the ease of decomposition of $\text{Pb}(\text{NO}_3)_2$ would compare to that of $\text{Ba}(\text{NO}_3)_2$. Explain your answer. You may find it useful to refer to the Data Booklet.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Barium ethanedioate, $\text{BaC}_2\text{O}_4$, decomposes on heating to produce barium oxide and a mixture of two different gases.

Construct an equation for the decomposition of barium ethanedioate.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
An impure sample of $\text{BaC}_2\text{O}_4$, of mass $0.500\text{ g}$, is added to $50.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.0200\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-(\text{aq})$, an excess. A redox reaction takes place and all the $\text{BaC}_2\text{O}_4$ reacts.

The resulting solution, containing unreacted acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$, is titrated with $0.0500\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Fe}^{2+}(\text{aq})$.

The end-point is reached when $30.40\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.0500\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Fe}^{2+}(\text{aq})$ has been added.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Calculate the percentage by mass of $\text{BaC}_2\text{O}_4$ in the $0.500\text{ g}$ impure sample. Show your working.
[$M_\text{r}$: $\text{BaC}_2\text{O}_4$, 225.3]

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Barium hydroxide, $\text{Ba}(\text{OH})_2$, is completely dissociated in aqueous solution.

Calculate the pH of $0.120\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Ba}(\text{OH})_2(\text{aq})$ at $298\text{ K}$.
